Atque ob id talis Diaboli subditus non solum stupenda quædam præstare poterit, sed etiam illi quibus hoc revelabit eadem præstabunt; quo paɖto fiet ut, Deo sic volente, tandem hæc arcana ita divulgentur, ut etiam absque conditione illa, qua omnium primus aut etiam primi hanc revelationem suscipere debuerunt, plures ea comperta habeant. Non aliter uti Chymicus v. gr. arcanissima quædam suo servo communicat ea conditione,ut ultra constitutum tempus servitus ejus extendatur, at servus illa aliis rursus communicat absque ulla tali aut quavis alia conditione, quopaɖto hi, nec isti servo, nec Domino ejus vel ad minimum tenentur.
units.tr: Furthermore, so that we may put aside our prejudices, it may well be noted here that, since the Devil has a thorough and intimate knowledge of the whole nature of things, he can disclose to one of his bondsmen certain amazing secrets of Nature, even though he does not add the causes by which these or those things come about. For this reason such a subject of the Devil will not only be able to perform certain wonderful feats, but those to whom he reveals this will also perform the same. In this way it will happen that, God so willing, these secrets are at last spread abroad so widely that many have learned them, even without the condition under which the first recipients or the first of them were bound to receive this revelation. It is much as when a Chymist, for example, communicates some most secret matters to his servant on the condition that the servant's bondage be extended beyond the appointed time; but the servant in turn communicates them to others without any such condition or any other, so that these others are bound neither to that servant nor to his master, at least not in any way.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Sic v. gr. posito, quòd olim Diabolus cuidam suorum servorum, ut eum magis obligaret revelârit, lapidem illum, quem nunc magnetem vocamus, miras tales virtutes habere, quibus stupenda da & excellentissima effici possunt; pœoniæ radicem aut glossopetram contra epilepsiam esse specificum; vitriolum certo modo calcinatum posse vulnera indistans curare, unde famosus ille pulvis sympatheticus exsurgit. Et similia infinita, quorum causæ naturales esse possunt, etsi illas nulla humana mens forsan unquam assequuta est aut assequtur.
units.tr: Thus, for example, let it be supposed that the Devil once revealed to one of his servants, in order to bind him more closely, that the stone we now call the magnet has such wonderful powers that by it stupendous and most excellent effects can be produced; that the root of the peony or the glossopetra is a specific against epilepsy; that vitriol calcined in a certain way can heal wounds at a distance, whence that famous sympathetic powder arises. And there are countless similar things, whose causes may be natural, although perhaps no human mind has ever grasped or will ever grasp them.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Si quis ergo tales revelationes à talibus hominibus aliisve absque ulla conditione & cerimonia superstitiosa & specie vanitatis communicatas acceperit, aliisque tradiderit, sic ut hodierni homines ex nuda relatione, etiam publicis typis facta, promiscuè talia cognita habeat, an judicandum homines qui talibus in suum commodum utuntur esse magos aut Diabolo obstrictos? Vereor ne nimis præcipitantes nostrum judicium, graviter peccaremus contra legemd charitatis à Christo latam: Ne judicate & non judicabimini, ne condemnate & non-damnabimini. Nam annon summe ridicula esset talis conclusio: Ego qui scientia rerum naturalium aut nullo modo aut saltem superfi-ciariè tinctus sum, nescio quomodo hæc & illa fiant, Ergo fiunt ex compactu cum Diabolo? Et confequenter, quia capere non possum quomodo per magnetem, poeoniam, pulverem fympatheticum, celerrimos manuum vel totius corporis motus, per automata multa artificiosissima &c : & quid ni etiam per omnia fere medicamenta, per Chymiam, artesque diversas hæc & illa homines faciunt, etsi leviffima & alliis optimè perspecta sint, Ergo informatione, ope, consilio & auxilio Diaboli faciunt ? Anticyram quidem talis mittendus effet, sed quàm multos haberet itineris fociosî Quippe, experientiâ undique conclamante, uti paucissimi hominum fiunt, qui nihil Diabolo aflcribunt, sic contrà innumeri sunt, qui omnia quæ ob imbecillitatem ingenii fui capere nequiunt, aut Diabolo aflcribunt; aut saltem,quæ mysteria naturæ ipsi explicare non possunt, aliorumque ingenia ad fui modum dimetiuntur, nescio ad quæ non fupcrnaturalia, miracula, Dei potentiam extraordinariam,& similia ex infantiæ præjudiciis effecta referant. Quod sane præjudicium priori multò crassius est, & ignorantiam rerum naturalium spissam, & plerumque vilem animum notat. Nam etsi nullus omninò mortalium dicta caperet, tamen nullo modo hæc sequentur, quæ superius notavimus, quia eo ipso dum fiunt, naturaliter fiunt, juxta Exc. I. c. I. §. 12. At unde de compactu cum Diabolo constabit, nisi ex aliis signis? Quae autem afferri solent plerumque non sunt infallibilia.
units.tr: If anyone, therefore, has received such revelations from such men or others, communicated without any condition, superstitious ceremony or appearance of vanity, and has passed them on, so that people today, from the bare report, even one published in print, possess such things indiscriminately, are we to judge that men who use such things for their own advantage are magicians or bound to the Devil? I fear that, judging too hastily, we would sin gravely against the law of charity laid down by Christ: "Judge not, and you shall not be judged; condemn not, and you shall not be condemned." For would not this conclusion be utterly ridiculous: "I, who am either not at all or only superficially versed in the science of natural things, do not know how these and those things are done; therefore they are done by a compact with the Devil"? And consequently, because I cannot understand how men produce these and those effects by the magnet, the peony, the sympathetic powder, the very swift movements of the hands or of the whole body, by many most artificial automata, and so on; and why not also by nearly all medicines, by chemistry, and by various arts, even those that are very slight and well understood by others; therefore they do these things by the information, help, counsel and aid of the Devil? Such a man would indeed deserve to be sent to Anticyra, but how many companions of the journey he would have! For while experience cries out on all sides, just as very few men are found who attribute nothing to the Devil, so on the contrary there are innumerable people who attribute to the Devil, or at least to supernatural causes, miracles, the extraordinary power of God and similar things, all that they cannot grasp because of the weakness of their own wit, or that they cannot explain themselves, measuring the minds of others by their own measure, and referring these things to prejudices of infancy. This prejudice is surely much grosser than the former, and it marks a dense ignorance of natural things and a generally base spirit. For even if no mortal at all understood these things, nevertheless the following points, which we noted above, would in no way follow: because by the very fact that they happen, they happen naturally, according to Exc. I, c. I, §. 12. But how shall it be established that there is a compact with the Devil, unless from other signs? And the signs usually brought forward are for the most part not infallible.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Sed, ut tandem poi tum (ad quem dudum adspiravimus) intremus, non pnto facile quid in historiis de operibus Diabolicis relatum inveniri, saltem quod verum est, cujus non ex dictis causam aliquam generalem dare possemus, quamvis ad valde particularia nunquam forsan penetrare possimus. Unice hoc Lectorem obnixe rogare debeo, ne antequam hos rudiores nostros conceptus bene perceperit, immaturum de illis judicium, cum lege charitatis & rationis non conveniens, stringere velit. Interim omnium nostrum erit, ut quo à Diaboli operibus non solum passive ledetiam active (ut cum scholis loquar) simus liberi, hoc est, ut Diaboli opera nec aliquam nobis noxam inferant, nec nos ejus instrumenta fiamus, quibus voluntatem suam exequatur, imprimis in vera Dei Triuni recta cognitione multum diuq; nos exercemus, ut in Summi hujus Boni contemplatione nos oblectantes, ejus pulcritudine & luce occupati, illud stupeamus, adoremus laudemus, & totos nos ipsi tradamus.
units.tr: But, to finally enter upon the matter (for which we have long been longing), it is not easy to find in histories anything reported about diabolical works, at least anything that is true, whose general cause we could not give from what has been said, although we may perhaps never be able to penetrate into very particular matters. I must earnestly ask the reader only this: that before he has well grasped these rather rough conceptions of ours, he should not wish to pass an immature judgment on them, one that does not agree with the law of charity and of reason. Meanwhile it will be the concern of all of us that we be free from the works of the Devil not only passively but also actively (to speak with the schools), that is, that the works of the Devil neither inflict any harm upon us nor make us its instruments by which it carries out its will; and above all we should exercise ourselves much and long in the true and right knowledge of the triune God, so that, delighting in the contemplation of this highest Good, occupied with its beauty and light, we may be astonished by it, adore it, praise it, and give ourselves wholly up to it.

units.la: Tum in naturalium rerum & nostri ipfius accurata magis cognitione, ut omnium, quæ ullo sensu evenire percipimus, causam aliquam naturalem & ordinariam quomodocunque etiam probabilem concipamus, ne omnia fpeëtris & præstigiis ascribamus. Et denique ut illas passiones occasionesque omnes fugiamus, quibus Diabolus nostræ crudelitati laqueos tendit, quibusque innexos ad regnum suum perducere valet. Quod feliciter ut cuivis succedat fecit PATER ISTE OMNIS LUMINIS & GRATIÆ & ANGELUS ILLE MAGNUS FOEDERIS, & SPIRITUS OMNIS VERITATIS, QUI TESTIFICATUR SPIRITUI NOSTRO NOS ESSE DEI FILIOS. DEUS TRIUNUS & BENEDICTUS,
units.tr: Then, by a more accurate knowledge of natural things and of ourselves, so that we may conceive of some natural and ordinary cause, however probable, for all those things which we perceive to happen through any sense, and not ascribe everything to apparitions and illusions. And finally, that we may flee all those passions and occasions by which the Devil lays snares for our cruelty, and by which he is able to lead those caught in them to his kingdom. May that FATHER OF ALL LIGHT and of GRACE, and that GREAT ANGEL OF THE COVENANT, and that SPIRIT OF ALL TRUTH, who bears witness to our spirit that we are children of God, grant this happily to everyone. THE TRIUNE and BLESSED GOD,

units.la: CUI UNICO SIT OMNIS LAUS & GLORIA IN OMNIA SECULA.
units.tr: TO WHOM ALONE BE ALL PRAISE AND GLORY FOREVER AND EVER.

units.la: Wittichius in Exercit: de statu hu- miliationis & exaltat: Christi §. 55. in medio.
units.tr: Wittichius in Exercitationes de statu humiliationis et exaltationis Christi, §. 55, in the middle.

units.la: Olim Deus concessit Diabolo potestatem in corpus Jobi, hoc excepto, ut parceret vitæ & animæ. At hic Deus videtur omnibus furiis concessisse potestatem illimitatam in ejus animam, quam infestarent omnibus viribus & modis, sciens eam tanto robore armatam, ut possçt istas omnes tentationes vincere & superare. Quomodo verò Diabolus animæ Christi dolores intulerit, difficilius est explicare. Quomodo per instrumenta sua, Judæos, milites, Herodem & Pilatum ægre fecerit corpori, ejus, facile potest intelligi. Etiam[?] interveniente corpore cruciare posse homines, docent exempla tot daemoniacorum, de quibus in historia Evangelica est mentio, speciatim filiæ Chananeæ mulieris, de quâ Math. xv, mater ipsius ἡ θυγάτηρ μου κακῶς δαιμονίζεται, & Luc. ix. 39. pater daemoniaci: Et ecce Spiritus apprehendit eum, & ipse repente clamat & dilaniat eum spumantem, & vix abscedit ab eo conterens eum. Quo etiam facit exemplum Jobi, quem percussit Satanas ulcere pessimo a planta pedis ejus usque ad verticem ejus. Job. II. 7. An vero Satanas Christi sanctissimam animam immediate affligere potuerit, dubitari posse videtur.
units.tr: Of old God granted the Devil power over the body of Job, with this exception, that he should spare his life and soul. But here God seems to have granted to all the furies unlimited power over his soul, which they might assail with every force and means, knowing that it was armed with such strength that it could conquer and overcome all these temptations. How the Devil inflicted pains on the soul of Christ is more difficult to explain. How he afflicted Christ's body through his instruments, the Jews, the soldiers, Herod and Pilate, can easily be understood. That the Devil can also torment men through the intervention of the body is taught by the many examples of demoniacs mentioned in the Gospel history, especially the daughter of the Canaanite woman in Matthew 15, whose mother says: "My daughter is grievously possessed by a devil" [ἡ θυγάτηρ μου κακῶς δαιμονίζεται], and Luke 9:39, the father of the demoniac: "And behold, a spirit taketh him, and he suddenly crieth out; and it teareth him that he foameth again, and bruising him hardly departeth from him." To this also belongs the example of Job, whom "Satan smote with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown." Job 2:7. Whether indeed Satan could afflict the most holy soul of Christ immediately seems open to doubt.

units.la: LVI. Sed id, quod Eph. II. 2. dicitur, principem potestatis aëris operarium filiis inobedientiæ, docet nos, diabolum in gentibus non conversis ad Deum efficacem esse in excitandis & fovendis concupiscentiis carnis v. 3. Quodque dicitur Johan. XIII. 2. diabolum injecisse in cor Judæ Simonis Iscariotæ, ut ipsum proderet, aliaque similia satis evincunt, etiam a Deo concedi Diabolo in hominum animas potestatem. Sive autem id mediate fieri dicas, interveniente phantasiâ, sive immediate, res mihi semper eodem redire videtur. Quantum enim attinet ad realitatem quamcunque, eam a Deo solo dependere & effici cum omnibus Theologis statuimus. Quando tamen Deo placet uti creaturarum interventu, & certo cuidam ordini se alligare, ut non nisi hoc prius facto efficiat posterius, v. gr. ut morbos hos vel illos curet non nisi intervenientibus certis quibusdam medicamentis, & quæ similia sunt, recte dicuntur illa, quæ sic intervenient, causæ
units.tr: LVI. But what is said in Ephesians 2:2, that the prince of the power of the air is "the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience," teaches us that the devil is effective in stirring up and fostering the lusts of the flesh in those Gentiles who are not converted to God (v. 3). And what is said in John 13:2, that the devil "put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, to betray him," and other similar passages, sufficiently prove that God also grants the Devil power over the souls of men. Whether you say this happens mediately, through the intervention of the imagination, or immediately, the matter always seems to me to come to the same thing. For as far as any reality whatever is concerned, we hold with all theologians that it depends solely on God and is effected by him. When, however, it pleases God to use the agency of creatures, and to bind himself to a certain order, so that he brings about the latter only after the former has been done, for example, that he heals these or those diseases only through the intervention of certain medicines, and things of that kind, then those things which intervene in this way are rightly called

units.la: . causæ fecundæ. Jam vero, etiam Diabolo in quibusdam Deum uti, tanquam causâ fecundâ, in prioribus visum fuit, 'quod tamen eo semper peragitur modo à divinâ providentiâ, ut culpa omnis ad diabolum & homines redundet, Deus verò nullius mali turpis aut criminis exin queat accusari.
units.tr: secondary causes. Now indeed, it was thought in earlier times that God also uses the Devil in certain matters as a secondary cause; yet this is always carried out by divine providence in such a way that all the guilt falls on the devil and on men, while God cannot be accused of any evil, base or criminal act arising from it.

units.la: LVII. Nihil verò repugnat, suppofito quòd Deus uti Diabolo in homine vel affligendo vel etiam ad peccatum incitando velit (quo exemplum Davidis facit, confer 2 Sam. xxix. cum 1 Chron. xxi. 1.) ut immediatè ei concedat potestatem in animam fine interveniente phantasiâ certoque motu fpirituum, cùm id æque facilè queat concipi, ac fi operationem certam ejus in certas corporis partes supponas. Cum enim in diabolo, mero spiritu, five merâ mente, à commercio corporis liberâ, nihil aliud possit concipi, præter intellectum & voluntatem, cui posteriori foli actiones adscribere convenit, non difficilius erit repræsentare animo, quomodo, posita ejus voluntate hoc vel illud efficiendi in hominis mente, id in istâ mente sequi possit, sola hac voluntate posita, ac quomodo, eadem ista voluntate posita, sequatur talis motus spirituum in hominis corpore. pore, post quem talis in anima fequatur cogitatio. Non enim major est ex natura rei connexio hujus quam illius cum altero. Quin imo difficilius aliquanto videtur intelligere, quomodo posita tali voluntate diaboli sequatur talis motus in corpore, & posito tali motu in corpore hominis sequatur talis in eodem cogitatio, quàm quomodo posita tali Satanae voluntate, sequatur talis in homine cogitatio.
units.tr: LVII. Nothing, however, stands in the way, supposing that God wishes to use the Devil in afflicting a man, or even in inciting him to sin (to which the example of David belongs; compare 2 Sam. 24 with 1 Chron. 21:1), that he should immediately grant him power over the soul without the intervention of the imagination and a certain motion of the spirits, since this can be conceived just as easily as if you supposed a certain operation of his upon certain parts of the body. For since in the devil, who is pure spirit, or pure mind, free from any commerce with a body, nothing else can be conceived beyond intellect and will, to which latter alone it is proper to ascribe actions, it will not be more difficult to picture in the mind how, once his will to effect this or that in the mind of a man is posited, that effect can follow in that mind by this will alone; and how, with that same will posited, such a motion of the spirits follows in the man's body, after which such a thought follows in the soul. For the connection of the one with the other is no greater from the nature of the thing than the connection of this with that. Indeed, it seems somewhat more difficult to understand how, with such a will of the devil posited, such a motion follows in the body, and with such a motion in the body of a man posited, such a thought follows in the same man, than how, with such a will of Satan posited, such a thought follows in a man.

units.la: LVIII. Quibus praemissis non difficile erit cogitare, quomodo fieri potuerit, ut Diabolus immediatè ani- mam Christi cruciaret & torqueret. Modum tamen speciali m determinare non praesumimus, dum hoc expendendum relinquimus &c: Reliqua h. l. legefis in ipsa Exercit: Wittichiana.
units.tr: LVIII. With these things premised, it will not be difficult to consider how it could have come about that the Devil immediately afflicted and tormented the soul of Christ. We do not, however, presume to determine the particular mode, since we leave this for consideration. The rest of this matter may be read in the Wittichian Exercitation itself.
